title: Chapter 27: The Malevolent 5
content:
Chapter 27

Taking in that painfully stiff posture, Wei Wuxian blinked. A spark of pure, mischievous trouble flared in his chest, and he was just about to let loose with some teasing when the sudden clatter of breaking porcelain shattered the quiet.

Both men snapped to their feet.

Across the room, the teacup and pot had shattered into a mess of white shards, steaming tea washing across the floorboards. Slumped right in the middle of the wreckage was an Evil-Quelling Qiankun pouch. Its fabric was thrashing violently, swelling and warping as whatever was trapped inside battered frantically against the seams, desperate to break out.

Though barely the size of a man’s palm, the pouch was enchanted with vast spatial pockets, reinforced inside and out with layers of intricate warding scripts and binding seals. Lan Wangji had locked the severed arm inside, weighing it down beneath a heavy teacup on the table, but seeing it go berserk jogged his memory: it was time for their nightly duet ofRest. Without that daily dose of calming music, even a top-tier pouch like this wouldn't hold the severed hand for long.

Wei Wuxian reached for his sash on reflex, but his fingers brushed empty air. Looking up, he found his crude bamboo flute resting in Lan Wangji’s pale hands. The man’s chin was dipped, carving into the rough wood with calm, painstaking precision before holding it out. Taking it back, Wei Wuxian noticed the ragged edges around the finger holes had been planed smooth, the rough finish polished into something remarkably neat.

"Play it properly," Lan Wangji said, his voice flat.

Remembering their chaotic performance back in the Spirit Hall—a screeching, off-key mess so offensive it had literally shocked Lan Qiren awake from a coma, only to make him vomit blood and pass right back out—Wei Wuxian almost doubled over laughing.God bless him, how did he stomach my noise for this long?

Deciding to play nice for once, he raised the polished bamboo to his lips with deadpan seriousness. Yet he’d barely cleared two clean notes when the Qiankun pouch suddenly puffed up like a sail, vaulting straight onto its base!

Wei Wuxian sputtered, blowing a sharp squeak through the mouthpiece. "What's its problem? Got so used to my dying-pig whistle that a little actual music offends its delicate ears?"

As if taking the insult personally, the pouch launched itself straight at his face!

Lan Wangji’s fingertips swept downward across the guqin with razor precision. All seven strings shuddered as one, unleashing a concussive, mountainous roar that slammed into the pouch like an invisible wall, knocking it flat against the floorboards.

Unfazed, Wei Wuxian picked the melody back up without missing a beat. Lan Wangji’s wrist softened, seamlessly guiding the harsh spiritual reprimand into the tranquil, soothing cadence ofRest, their notes braiding together in seamless harmony.

As the final note dissolved, the pouch deflated to its normal size, lying completely dormant.

Tucking the flute away, Wei Wuxian frowned down at it. "It's never been this erratic before. Something definitely set it off."

Lan Wangji gave a slight nod, his gaze shifting up to meet his. "Something on you."

Wei Wuxian glanced down at himself on reflex. He’d only picked up one new souvenir today: the Malignant Curse Mark he’d siphoned off Jin Ling.

And Jin Ling had contracted that curse inside the stone fortresses on Xinglu Ridge. If the severed arm was losing its mind over that exact residue, that meant...

"You think other pieces of its corpse are buried in the walls of the Nie Clan's blade vault?" Wei Wuxian asked.

The next morning, before the mist had cleared, the two set off toward Xinglu Ridge once more.

Having been caught red-handed and spilling his guts the night before, Nie Huaisang had dragged his trusted retainers out in the dead of night to scrub the crime scene clean. By the time Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji strolled up to the clearing, the man had just finished supervising the repairs on the wall Jin Ling had been extracted from—slotting a fresh corpse into the cavity and sealing it behind layers of pristine white bricks.

He was vigorously dabbing the sweat from his brow when he turned, his knees instantly giving out at the sight of the newcomers. Forcing an agonizingly tight smile, he stammered, "H-Hanguang-jun... and, uh, you..."

Wei Wuxian waved cheerily. "Morning, Sect Leader Nie! Laying bricks, are we?"

Nie Huaisang scrubbed his forehead with a handkerchief so hard he was practically peeling off skin. "Yes, yes, quite..."

Looking at him with nine parts pity and one part theatrical guilt, Wei Wuxian sighed. "Hate to be the bearer of bad news, but... you might need to lay them all over again in a minute."

"Yes, yes, of course—wait, WHAT?!"

Shing!

Bichen slipped from its scabbard. Nie Huaisang watched in pure, helpless horror as the masonry he’d spent hours finishing cracked clean down the seams.

Tearing things down was always infinitely faster than building them back up. Wei Wuxian pried loose stone blocks with terrifying efficiency, moving twice as fast as the masons had. Nie Huaisang clutched his fan, trembling like a leaf in an autumn gale, tears of pure, unadulterated frustration pricking his eyes. But with Hanguang-jun standing guard like a wall of ice, he didn't dare squeak a word of protest.

When Lan Wangji laid out their deductions in a few clipped sentences, Nie Huaisang threw his hands toward the sky, swearing frantically: "Impossible! Absolutely impossible! Every body we source for the vault is intact—we don't take mutilated corpses, and definitely no men missing their left arms! If you don't believe me, I'll help you tear the wall down myself to prove it! Just... please, put it back together as soon as you're done! We can't leave it open; this is my ancestral shrine!"

With several Nie disciples pitching in, Wei Wuxian stepped back to let the manpower do the heavy lifting.

Within half an hour, most of the masonry encasing Jin Ling's original burial spot had been stripped bare. The disciples pulled black cloth masks over their noses or popped herbal pills to suppress their living scent, ensuring their breath wouldn't trigger a mass reanimation. From the dark, compacted earth, pale hands, vein-ridged feet, and mats of greasy hair emerged one by one. Every male corpse was scraped clean of mud and laid out in neat rows across the clearing.

Some were stripped down to dry skeletons, some were mid-decay, and others looked freshly dead. Yet all of them shared one crucial trait: every single body possessed all four limbs. Not a single one-armed male corpse was in sight.

Nie Huaisang fidgeted, speaking in an anxious whisper. "This wall should be enough, right? We don't need to knock down the rest, do we? Surely not."

It was indeed enough. The curse mark on Jin Ling had been pitch-black, meaning whatever had branded him had been packed in right next to him. It wouldn't have strayed beyond this section of brick.

Wei Wuxian squatted by the row of stiffs, his brows knitting together.

Lan Wangji looked down. "Release the pouch?"

Letting the severed left hand out so it could sniff out its own flesh wasn't a terrible idea. The problem was, if it got too close to its missing parts, the sheer surge of resonant malice might trigger an explosive reaction they couldn't contain. Deep inside a tomb saturated with corpse-gas, the danger was amplified tenfold—which was the entire reason they’d waited for daylight to dig.

Wei Wuxian shook his head, racking his brain. "Could that arm belong to a woman? No, I can tell a man's hand from a woman's in my sleep... Don't tell me the guy had three arms?!"

He barely had time to snort at his own absurd joke before Lan Wangji spoke up: "Legs."

The word hit Wei Wuxian like a splash of water. He’d completely overlooked it: the curse mark on Jin Ling had been restricted entirely to his legs!

"Strip their pants!" Wei Wuxian yelled, jumping up. "Drop their trousers, quick!"

Nie Huaisang looked ready to faint from mortification. "How can you shout such vulgar filth right in front of Hanguang-jun?!"

"What's vulgar about it? We're all guys here," Wei Wuxian fired back, already reaching for the nearest belt. "Lend a hand! Strip their trousers! Leave the women alone, just the men!"

Poor Nie Huaisang couldn't believe his life. Spilling the clan's darkest secrets yesterday was bad enough; now he was being forced to desecrate corpses by pulling their pants down inside his ancestors' sacred shrine! He was convinced that the moment he died, generations of Nie ancestors would line up in the underworld to slap him raw, cursing him to be born crippled in his next life. Tears welled up in his eyes.

Thankfully, Lan Wangji stepped in, catching Wei Wuxian’s wrist.

Nie Huaisang was just about to silently praise Hanguang-jun’s pristine virtue when the man spoke: "I will do it."

Wei Wuxian blinked. "You? You're really going to touch that?"

Lan Wangji’s brow gave a faint, twitching pulse, as if testing the absolute limits of his endurance. "Do not move," he repeated, voice tight. "I will handle it."

Within moments, Lan Wangji paused. "Found it."

The crowd surged forward. Resting right beside Lan Wangji’s white boots was a male corpse with faint, pale rings circling both of its upper thighs. Dense, tiny stitches of flesh-colored thread held the seams together. Above the line, the skin tone was noticeably different from the tone below.

The legs didn't belong to the torso at all.

They had been grafted on—neatly stitched into place by hand!

Nie Huaisang stood completely frozen, his mouth hanging open.

Wei Wuxian turned to him. "Who handles sourcing and inspecting the corpses for the vault?"

"Usually... usually the clan leaders curate and stockpile them personally during their lifetimes," Nie Huaisang rambled, his thoughts spinning out of control. "My brother passed away so suddenly he didn't leave enough, so I helped gather a few... But I only accepted bodies that had all their limbs and features intact! That's all I looked for! I swear I don't know anything else..."

Interrogating him was a dead end; figuring out who had smuggled this stitched patchwork into the masonry was impossible right now. Between the middlemen who sold the bodies and the internal disciples managing the vault, the suspect list stretched into infinity. The only way to crack the truth was to track down the rest of the pieces, assemble the corpse, and summon the complete soul.

After much hassle, they carefully severed the stitched legs from the torso. Shoving the limbs into a fresh Qiankun pouch, Wei Wuxian glanced at Lan Wangji. "Looks like our friend here was drawn and quartered. Not just butchered, but scattered across the realm—a piece hidden here, a scrap tossed there. Talk about a grudge. Let's just pray they didn't mince him into too many little pieces."

Parting ways, Nie Huaisang offered a polite "until we meet again," though the sheer, lingering dread painted across his face screamed that he prayed to heaven they would never cross paths for the rest of his natural life.

Returning to the inn, Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji barred the door and brought all three severed pieces out for a closer look.

Sure enough, the skin tone of the legs matched the severed left hand down to the pore. Laid out near each other, the limbs began to tremble violently, twitching as if trying to fuse back together, frustrated only by the yawning void where the torso should have been. They unquestionably belonged to the same man.

Aside from confirming that the victim had been tall, muscular, broad-shouldered, and gifted with terrifyingly high cultivation, they were still completely in the dark.

Fortunately, the severed hand didn't leave them guessing for long. Its pale fingers snapped rigid, locking its bearing onto a new heading: Southwest.

Tracing the phantom's compass, Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji set out toward the city of Yueyang.
